P1.evidence: 'I already saw like your application' — he had read it but did not read anything back, so the prospect got no sense of being seen. Frame was again three parts: 'go through where you're at, where you want to go. If it's a good fit, perfect. We'll get you started. If not... I'll point you in the best direction.' Agreement obtained and the open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Best baseline in the batch. Age asked ('how old are you actually at the moment?' — 40). Desk-bound work established properly, including hours seated and daily step count ('you sit, how much do you sit a day, like eight, ten hours?' and 'How much steps do you think you get in?'). Health conditions asked directly — 'Any injuries or something you should know about?' — which is what produced the scoliosis and hyperlordosis disclosure. Current training and other movement both asked. Diet interrogated thoroughly: home vs out, frequency, and what he actually orders. Still missing: height and weight never asked despite muscle-gain and fat-loss goals, duration of the tightness never established, and neither sleep nor energy asked at all.

P3.evidence: Aesthetic target pinned down ('you don't want to become big and buff, but more so?' — 'No, I do want to stay lean... I want to build my shoulders up, have a nice chest'). The bridge to the real driver ran — 'What's the real reason for you?' — and the 91-year-old father came out as the longevity motive. Who-else-does-it-impact was asked honestly and honestly answered ('no partner or anything'), so the rep correctly redirected to self. Reflect-back ran: 'your big why sounds like really that longevity aspect.' Only the something-you-can't-do-physically question is absent.

P4.evidence: 'Have you tried anything else besides the gym already?' and 'When did you sort of come to that idea for yourself?' produced the whole history — two years of gym, a mobility-focused trainer who then left the country. The blocker was isolated precisely: 'Do you feel like it's impossible to find the time, or is it mainly the time traveling to the gym that sort of gets wasted?' The prospect named the gap himself: 'I feel like I also don't have the knowledge of what to do.' The scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line never ran.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran cleanly — 'do you feel like you would be willing to settle for when you're 41 and nothing really changed?' — but the horizon was two months to his birthday, not the scripted two years, so the cost of inaction never accumulated any weight. No 'why not?' and no line in the sand. This is the phase that would have carried the price, and its absence is visible: when $6,000 landed, the prospect had no emotional counterweight and went straight to comparison shopping.

P6.evidence: Both commitment questions ran before the offer. Belief: 'do you feel like when we get all of that in place, you're going to be able to get to the goal of... getting more mobility, getting in better shape, but then also in the long run, just having that longevity?' — 'Yeah, yeah, it sounds like it could be something that would fit.' Blocker sweep ran earlier at 00:18:00: 'Anything else, personally, stopping you from getting to the outcome, or not really?' P6c is partial because the yes was soft ('it sounds like it could be') and, when hesitation duly surfaced at price, the rep did not return to Phase 5 as instructed — he made a commercial concession instead.

P11.evidence: All four steps completed and confirmed before hanging up, which no other call in this batch achieved. Payment taken live and verified both ways ('I did the payment as well' / 'the payment I saw come true'). Trevor call booked for Monday 3:15pm Pacific with the invite confirmed received. Agreement email confirmed arrived and signed on the call ('I finished the agreement'). Welcome email, Skool access and the onboarding questionnaire all walked through, with the rep chasing the Skool access specifically: 'log into Skool, because when you do that, then the team gets a notification... let me know if you haven't gotten access by late today, then I'll push the team for it.'

objection_plays.detail: 'I'll think about it, and I can let you know via text message' at 00:33:56. The rep refused the deferral, which is the right instinct, and asked the substance of the first OA move — 'do you feel like it is something you feel like, yeah, you see yourself doing this?' — then kept excavating until the real blocker appeared. None of the scripted lines ran: no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no identity close.

Isolation ran twice and correctly — 'outside of the investment, do you feel like, yeah, this is what would help you get to that outcome still?' and 'it sounds like it's just about the investments. Is that correct?' Not a single financial-picture question ran: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. In fairness the diagnosis was right — this was never affordability, it was value comparison — but the play was not run.

Clear fear/doubt trigger: 'I'm kind of stuck with it for six months' and the worry that it would not feel personalised. The rep named the emotion in substance ('a little bit of stress around making the decision for yourself'), which is adjacent to 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty?', and ran a genuinely good improvised reframe — asking whether he could verify personalisation with an in-home trainer either, before starting. But none of the scripted bridges ran (no BRIDGE, no PLANE, no BURNED BEFORE), and the objection was ultimately closed with money rather than with conviction: a one-month trial invented on the spot.

SCRIPT GAP — the 'a cheaper alternative might be better value' gap again, here in its comparison-shopping form: 'if I spent 6k on that, what would that look like? How many sessions would that be?' The prospect wanted a per-session unit-economics comparison against an in-home personal trainer. There is no scripted value framing for $6,000 against N sessions, and the rep had to invent the entire response. Worth building: he actually improvised the strongest available answer, which is that neither option's personalisation is verifiable in advance.

SCRIPT GAP — the prospect asked for a try-before-you-commit structure ('I would maybe just do one session. And then if I liked it, then maybe buy a pack of five') and there is no sanctioned answer, so the rep created a one-month trial and a new price point live. This is the second call in this batch where the absence of a scripted commercial fallback produced an improvised commercial term.

notes: The best-executed call in the batch on process: strongest P2, a properly run P3, a real P4 root cause, and the only complete P11 in ten files. The gap is P5 — the consequence frame was set at two months instead of two years, so nothing was holding the price up, and the objection was eventually resolved with an invented commercial concession rather than with the conviction that Phase 5 is supposed to build. Coach: run the two-year frame, and escalate the demand for a trial structure rather than inventing one.
